hypotheses.title: An unreadable registry lists nothing, so a registry template reads as not-catalog
hypotheses.why_not_a_finding: A working branch still requires a per-user token, token login equal to the repository owner, and a passing push probe. The only principal who can pass is the personal-account owner of that repository, who can already push to it with the same token. No boundary is crossed.
hypotheses.failure_direction: open, stated in the is_catalog_github_template docstring

hypotheses.title: A renamed catalog repository's old name reads as not-catalog
hypotheses.why_not_a_finding: Same bound as above: owner and catalog checks compare the typed name, and the owner check limits the grant to the repository's own personal-account owner. Whether GitHub redirects the push was not tested.
hypotheses.follow_up: compare the canonical full_name from the repository API in both checks

boundary_review.property: an agent never receives a working (push) branch on a repository its creator does not own
boundary_review.before: every per-user-token create from a github: template returned pull-only at the catalog branch; the owner check and push probe never ran
boundary_review.after: catalog membership is read from the admin list, else the registry, plus the bundled defaults; non-catalog repositories proceed to the owner check and push probe, unchanged
grant_conditions: not fork-to-own, source_mode not set explicitly, kind agent, not ephemeral
a token of tier per_user or per_agent
repository not in the catalog (case- and .git-insensitive)
token login equals repository owner, case-insensitive
boundary_review.widening: repositories the creator's own GitHub account owns and can push to
boundary_review.tightening: a respelled catalog repository (case, .git suffix) is still the catalog repository
